title: Additivity of unassisted classical capacity
source: Lovitz and Wu, Section~1.3, Eq.~(33), and the outlook of Zhu and Wang explicitly ask whether the fully regularized classical capacity can be superadditive \sourcecite{ref:rca-lovitz-wu}{LW26} \sourcecite{ref:rca-zhu-wang}{ZW26}.
progress: Using independent encodings establishes $C(\Phi\otimes\Psi)\geq C(\Phi)+C(\Psi)$. Shor's additivity theorem gives equality when one channel is entanglement breaking, meaning its output is separable from every reference system, because the same theorem applies to every tensor power of the channel pair \sourcecite{ref:rca-shor}{Sho02}.

Hastings exhibited a strict Holevo information violation for a pair at one use of each factor. Lovitz and Wu provide further deterministic and random examples and leave Eq.~\eqref{eq:rca-additivity} open \sourcecite{ref:rca-hastings}{Has09} \sourcecite{ref:rca-lovitz-wu}{LW26}.

Collins and Youn show nonadditivity of regularized minimum output entropy in an infinite-dimensional commuting-operator model. Kalantar and Shobeiri extend this line of examples within the same model. Equation~\eqref{eq:rca-additivity} concerns finite-dimensional channels \sourcecite{ref:rca-collins-youn}{CY22} \sourcecite{ref:rca-kalantar-shobeiri}{KS25}.

comment: A strict inequality for Eq.~\eqref{eq:rca-additivity} must compare the joint capacity with the separately regularized capacities. The catalog's \href{https://qiqc-op.com/problem/op_25e23d6e92ebce9d/}{closed-form witness question} uses the one-use quantity in Eq.~\eqref{eq:rca-holevo}.
